messages.subject: How to calcule MX metrics
parts:
Hi colleagues,

I would like to incorporate MX metrics in a new paper, following Rowlands' studies, where we want to represent physical activity through a radar plot.

I have two databases obtained from GGIR (part 2 and 5) and I would like to know how I can obtain the accumulated MX per day (specifically, the most active 2, 5, 15, 30, 60 and 120 min -M2, M5, M15, M30, M60 and M120, respectively--- and the most active 8 h (M1/3Day) to be able to make this radar plot.

Could someone who has done something related, point me in the right direction or help me to clarify this question?

Thank you very much for your help in advance

Have a nice day,

Sam.

messages.author: 5270e62a7d3ec577
messages.subject: Re: How to calcule MX metrics
parts:
Hi Sam,

To generate Mx acceleration values you need to specify the times in the qlevels function in part 2. Nathan Dawkins describes this in section 2.4.1 here: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/33459582.

So, for the Mx metrics you have specified you would need qlevels = c(c(480/1440),c(1320/1440),c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440),c(1425/1440),c(1435/1440),c(1438/1440)),
where M2 = c(1438/1440) and so on. These are outputted into part2 as a percentage, so M2 column name will be "p99.86111_ENMO_mg_0.24hr" and that is the lowest acceleration value for the most active 2 minutes of the 24h day which we display on the radar plots. Hope that makes sense

On a side note, as it's not specified in Rowlands 2019, we made the code accessible through Github to generate the radar plots the same way that we did. The repository can be found here with a detailed breakdown of instructions:
https://github.com/Maylor8/RadarPlotGenerator. 

Thanks,
Ben

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: How to calcule MX metrics
parts:
Hi Ben,

Could you propose a sentence or two that should be added to the GGIR documentation (vignette) about the MX metrics and how your GitHub repository aids this work? I believe there is no discussion of it at the moment.

Further, it may be good to highlight https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues/723 to you. MX has also been used in the context of circadian rhythm analyses but then focussed on most active consecutive hours (argument winhr in GGIR) rather than the non-consecutive MX you are familiar with. I am not sure a new accordnym is desirable, but we need to be more specific when discussing MX as this could at some point lead to misunderstandings.

Thanks, Vincent
